chunks: What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbbās, from Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about tawaf after al-ʿAṣr, and he said: Perform tawaf and pray two rakʿahs before salat al-Maghrib at sunset. And if you perform another tawaf, then pray the two rakʿahs after al-Maghrib. And I asked him about tawaf after al-Fajr, and he said: Perform tawaf until, when the sun has risen, then perform the rakʿahs.

key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: the ritual circumambulation around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْعَصْرِ: the ʿAṣr prayer time in relation to when tawaf is performed
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer time in relation to tawaf
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib prayer time, used here as a legal timing marker
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer prescribed after tawaf
key_terms.طَلَعَتِ: the rising of the sun, marking the time to perform the prayer

ai.seo_question: When should the two rakʿahs of tawaf be prayed if tawaf is performed after al-ʿAṣr or after al-Fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the time of the two rakʿahs connected to tawaf when tawaf is done after al-ʿAṣr or after al-Fajr. It indicates how the prayer of tawaf is timed around periods connected with sunset and sunrise, giving a practical legal ruling for worship during hajj or ʿumrah.
